body.statement: Every \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\) induces a coupling \(\pi\in\Pi_T(p)\) of the two factual responses. Conversely, every \(\pi\in\Pi_T(p)\) lifts by finite edgewise completion to a law \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\). Under this lift, the smallest attainable contribution of edge \((i,j)\) to \(\theta_{ab}\) is \(d^-(i,j)\), and therefore \(\inf_{q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)}\theta_{ab}(q)=\kappa-\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_T(p)}(\pi_{ss}+\pi_{tt})\).
body.justification: This is the structural reduction that turns the response-type projection into a two-diagonal transport problem.
body.gap: Song et al. couple each factual arm to a full vector of potential outcomes under global exclusion; they do not provide this direct two-arm partial-matching reduction under selected trust.
body.consumer: It supplies the proof engine for closed-form bounds and constructive response laws without enumerating \(|\mathcal E|^2 2^{|T|+2|U|}\) saturated types.
